A LIST OF ALIQUOT CYCLES OF LENGTH GREATER THAN 2

The number in the first column identifies the cycle; cycles are numbered
in increasing order of the smallest member.  The numbers in the second column
of the file are the numbers occurring in each aliquot cycle; the third column
contains the prime factorizations of the numbers in the second column.  The
aliquot cycles are separated by blank lines.  There are 5410 cycles in all:
5398 of length 4, 1 of length 5, 5 of length 6, 4 of length 8, 1 of length 9,
and 1 of length 28.

P. Moews and I have exhaustively searched for all aliquot cycles of length
greater than 2 such that the number preceding the largest number of the cycle
is below 1.54*10^11.  As of November 1997, Jan Otto Munch Pedersen
<amicable@post.cybercity.dk> had carried this search up to 4.27*10^11; as of
January 2001, he had carried it up to 4.5*10^11; as of February 2003, up
to 6*10^11; and as of July 2004, up to 6.1*10^11.  As of November 2005,
Andre Needham <andre_needham@hotmail.com> had carried this search up to
10^12; as of May 2006, up to 2*10^12; as of September 2006, up to 3*10^12;
as of November 2006, up to 4*10^12; and as of September 2007, up to 5*10^12.
As of October 2016, Dmitry Bodyagin has carried this search up to
10^14.  Also, as of August 2015, Dmitry Bodyagin has exhaustively searched
for all aliquot cycles whose smallest element is odd and is no larger than
10^15, and as of May 2016, a mersenneforum.org group has exhaustively
searched for all aliquot cycles whose smallest element is odd and is no
larger than 10^16, using a program designed by Dmitry Bodyagin.  All cycles
found are among those shown below.

Some of the cycles of length 4 are of a form given by Borho (see the
reference below) analogous to Euler's first form for amicable pairs.
These cycles are numbers 10, 22, 36, 40, 45, 65, 70, 75, 76, 79, 80, 82, 83,
85-87, 89, 92-94, and 102-5410.

(If two or more people seem to have independently discovered the same cycle,
it will be credited to both or all of them.)
